contributions.statement: When an LLM reviews code for cross-boundary contract bugs, require each alarm to be grounded in lexically retrieved real code (extract identifiers, then grep/LSP the actual definitions) before it is reported; removing that grounding step raised false positives from 13.9% to 60.5% and nearly halved real bugs found.
contributions.evidence: §IV-E Table IV: w/o ERG 17 bugs at 60.47% FP vs 31 at 13.89%; single target (PyTorch), single model (GPT-5.4), author-judged alarms. Upstream confirmation of 26 bugs (Table III) shows the full pipeline finds real defects.

reason: The retrieval-grounding ablation adds a measured false-positive magnitude for LLM static review on a real target with maintainer-confirmed bugs. Everything else is PyTorch/CUDA-specific and baselined against strawman analyzers.
